body.statement: Fix \(r\in\mathcal R_B\), \(C_v<\infty\), and \(\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A_{\mathrm{det}}\) whose pilot-measurable main-wave rate \(\widehat r_n\) converges locally uniformly in probability to \(r\). The strict slack \(\delta_q>0\) implies that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), every positive or negative tilt on \(\mathcal H\times\{v:\lVert v\rVert\le C_v\}\) lies in \(\mathcal M_\eta(p)\). Conditional on \(\mathscr P_n\), every fixed finite collection of points in that domain obeys the observed-data expansion \[\log\frac{d(\mathbb P^{\widehat r_n}_{p,q_n(h,v)})^{\otimes n}}{d(\mathbb P^{\widehat r_n}_{p,q^0})^{\otimes n}}(O_1,\ldots,O_n)=\Delta_n(s(h,v))-\tfrac12J_{\widehat r_n}(s(h,v),s(h,v))+\operatorname{rem}_{n,\widehat r_n}(h,v),\] where \(\sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}|\operatorname{rem}_{n,\widehat r_n}(h,v)|=o_{\mathbb P^{\widehat r_n}_{p,q^0}}(1)\). Under \(\mathbb P^{\widehat r_n}_{p,q^0}\), the conditional finite-coordinate law of \(\Delta_n\) converges to a centered Gaussian process with covariance \(J_r\), uniformly on that compact domain. The map \(\Pi_rs=\mathcal T_rA_{\mathrm{tan}}s\) is the \(J_r\)-orthogonal contrast projection, and under \(\mathbb P^{\widehat r_n}_{p,q_n(h,v)}\), \(U_{n,r}\Rightarrow N(h,\Sigma(r))\) uniformly on the same domain. The likelihood contribution from \(\mathscr P_n\), whose fully labeled pilot records satisfy \(R=1\) and \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=Y\), is asymptotically negligible because \(m_n/n\to0\). Consequently, for every finite prior on \(\mathcal H\), the infimum over all \(\psi_n\) of the prior regret along the least-favorable submodels \(q^0+\mathcal T_rh/\sqrt n\), which also remain in \(\mathcal M_\eta(p)\) for both signs and all sufficiently large \(n\) by the same slack argument, converges to the Bayes regret in \(Z\sim N(h,\Sigma(r))\); this finite-prior risk-transfer conclusion, rather than total-variation convergence of experiments, is the conclusion used downstream.
body.justification: The explicit conditional LAN expansion and finite-prior transfer identify exactly what survives a discontinuous pilot design and the complete contrast-preserving nuisance fiber.
body.gap: Hirano and Porter provide fixed-experiment scalar treatment-rule transfer, while Cook et al. provide stabilized adaptive AIPW Gaussianity; neither conditions on a pilot sigma-field to prove a design-indexed finite-coordinate LAN expansion and least-favorable finite-prior transfer over all outcome-shape tangents.
body.consumer: It licenses lower-risk transfer for any admissible prospective annotation procedure and prevents a restricted outcome family from determining the design.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(C_v<\infty\), and write \(s=s(h,v)\). The membership conclusion follows from \(\mathrm{thm:local\text{-}chart\text{-}membership}\). On its compact parameter set there is a finite \(A_C\) such that
\[
\max_{a,x,\ell}\left|\frac{s_{ax\ell}}{q^0_{ax\ell}}\right|\le A_C,
\]
because \(q^0_{ax\ell}\ge\eta>0\). Conditional on \(\mathscr P_n\), the annotation rate \(\widehat r_n\) is fixed. For one main-wave observation its likelihood ratio relative to \(q^0\) equals one when \(R=0\), and when \(R=1,Y^{\mathrm{obs}}=y_\ell\) it equals
\[
\frac{q^0_{AX\ell}+s_{AX\ell}/\sqrt n}{q^0_{AX\ell}}
=1+\frac{g_s(O)}{\sqrt n}.
\]
Annotation ignorability is what cancels the annotation factor. If \(A_C/\sqrt n\le1/2\), Taylor's formula with a uniform third-derivative bound gives
\[
\log(1+z)=z-\frac{z^2}{2}+r(z),\qquad |r(z)|\le\frac{2}{3}|z|^3,\qquad |z|\le\frac12.
\]
Summing this identity gives
\[
\log\Lambda_{n,\mathrm{main}}(s)
=\Delta_n(s)-\frac1{2n}\sum_{i=1}^ng_s(O_i)^2+R_n(s),
\qquad \sup_s|R_n(s)|\le\frac{2A_C^3}{3\sqrt n}.
\]
Choose a basis of the finite-dimensional space \(\mathcal E\). Every product of two basis scores is bounded. Conditional Chebyshev bounds for their sample averages, followed by the assumed locally uniform convergence \(\widehat r_n\to r\), imply
\[
\sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}
\left|\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^ng_s(O_i)^2-J_{\widehat r_n}(s,s)\right|=o_P(1).
\]
This proves the stated uniform remainder. Applied to the vector of basis scores, \(\mathrm{lem:finite\text{-}dimensional\text{-}lindeberg\text{-}feller}\) applies conditionally because the summands are centered, uniformly bounded, and their covariance converges to the matrix of \(J_r\). Linearity in the basis coordinates upgrades this to uniform finite-coordinate convergence over the compact tangent set.

For \(t\in\ker(A_{\mathrm{tan}})\), the information calculation gives
\[
J_r(\Pi_rs,t)=J_r(\mathcal T_rA_{\mathrm{tan}}s,t)
=(A_{\mathrm{tan}}s)^\top\Sigma(r)^{-1}A_{\mathrm{tan}}t=0,
\]
and \(A_{\mathrm{tan}}\Pi_rs=A_{\mathrm{tan}}s\). Thus \(\Pi_r\) is the \(J_r\)-orthogonal projection onto the least-favourable contrast space. Moreover, for every \(b\in\mathbb R^d\),
\[
J_r(\mathcal T_rb,s(h,v))=b^\top\Sigma(r)^{-1}h,
\qquad J_r(\mathcal T_rb,\mathcal T_rc)=b^\top\Sigma(r)^{-1}c.
\]
The proved joint likelihood and score convergence imply that, under the local law, \(\Delta_n\circ\mathcal T_r\) has limiting mean \(\Sigma(r)^{-1}h\) and covariance \(\Sigma(r)^{-1}\). Therefore \(U_{n,r}=\Sigma(r)(\Delta_n\circ\mathcal T_r)\Rightarrow N(h,\Sigma(r))\), uniformly on the fixed bounded fiber.

For a fully labelled pilot record the local likelihood ratio is \(1+g_s/\sqrt n\), and hence
\[
E_0\Lambda_{n,\mathrm{pilot}}(s)^2
=\left(1+\frac{J_1(s,s)}n\right)^{m_n}
\le \exp\{m_nJ_1(s,s)/n\}=1+o(1)
\]
uniformly on the compact tangent set, by \(m_n/n\to0\). Thus its total-variation contribution is at most one half of the square root of the displayed second-moment excess and vanishes. Conditional on every pilot realization,
\[
E_0\{\Lambda_{n,\mathrm{main}}(s)^2\mid\mathscr P_n\}
=\left(1+\frac{J_{\widehat r_n}(s,s)}n\right)^n
\le e^{J_1(s,s)},
\]
because \(0\le\widehat r_{n,ax}\le1\). The full likelihood vectors for any finite collection of local states are therefore uniformly square-integrable, regardless of discontinuities of the pilot selector.

For a finite prior \(\sum_{\nu=1}^Nw_\nu\delta_{h_\nu}\), take the allowed least-favourable tangents \(\mathcal T_rh_\nu\). Compactness of \(\mathcal H\) and continuity of \(\mathcal T_r\) place all of them in one fixed nuisance ball. Under the baseline law the optimal Bayes regret in the finite experiment is exactly
\[
E_0\min_{j\in[M]}\sum_{\nu=1}^Nw_\nu\ell_{\mathrm{reg}}(h_\nu,j)\Lambda_n(\mathcal T_rh_\nu).
\]
The integrand is continuous in the likelihood vector and is bounded by \(2\sup_{h\in\mathcal H}\lVert h\rVert_\infty\sum_\nu w_\nu\Lambda_n(\mathcal T_rh_\nu)\). Joint likelihood convergence and the preceding square-integrability therefore give convergence of its expectation. In the Gaussian limit the likelihood vector is that generated by \(Z\sim N(h,\Sigma(r))\), so the limit is precisely the asserted Gaussian Bayes regret. This proves the finite-prior transfer without claiming total-variation convergence of the discrete and Gaussian experiments.
